children: , the hybrid cloud, AI and mainframe company, brought its z17 mainframe to Marist University's new Innovation Incubator; shares climbed about 2.2% to $236.55 Wednesday morning from Tuesday's $231.38 close . The stock still sat 2.59% below its $242.84 GF Value estimate. That gap gives investors a valuation reference, but the campus project alone does not close it.

Marist plans to test autonomous marketing agents and explore AI applications in polling. Researchers are also scoping a project that would use quantum optimization to build portfolio allocations. IBM provided the machine for students and faculty to develop and test applications; its announcement gives no dollar value for the system or revenue forecast for the collaboration.

The investor case here takes patience. Getting future developers comfortable with IBM's technology could pay off if their work reaches enterprise customers. For now, the z17 at Marist shows where IBM wants its platform used. It does not yet show what customers will pay for the applications that emerge.

title: IBM Gains 2.2% as z17 Enters an Agentic AI Laboratory
